cells.tense: You're tending it now, and you know it.
cells.verb: Keeping the fire going — feeding what you've started without burning yourself down.
cells.place: Where the shape of things gets set — the one who decides how the work holds together.
cells.ask: Offer the next piece of momentum that isn't strictly yours to give — one thing you can dream forward because you've already lived the ground it stands on. What comes back is a fresh current moving through the structure you built.
cells.core: You're the one who keeps the thing going, and you do it by tending rather than forcing. The fire you've built is steady because you've learned how to hold space for it — enough to fuel it, not enough to burn it out. People keep going because they're near you, and you know that's part of what you do. That steadiness isn't passive. It's the whole engine.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the fire going by tending it, not by forcing it.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a future you can't write in — ahead of everyone, ahead of the timing.
cells.verb: Building the structure before anyone asked — organizing what hasn't arrived, holding the shape against the chaos you see coming.
cells.place: Where the pattern gets set — and you're setting it before the room is ready.
cells.ask: Invite one true thing you already know into the structure you're building, and let it calibrate the plan. What comes back is equilibrium — a centered presence that can hold complexity without gripping it.
cells.core: You're pushing the structure harder than anyone asked, because somewhere ahead there's a version where it all holds together and you're living in it. Every conversation becomes a chance to get them ahead of the curve. The control is costing you the thing control was for — the fire isn't being tended, it's being guarded from a future that hasn't happened. You're running ahead of the natural timing, and the timing is what you can't force.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the shape ahead of the timing, and the timing is what's slipping.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you — the fire went out and you didn't move.
cells.verb: Holding back the shape — not building, not organizing, just waiting for the ground to feel solid before you commit.
cells.place: Where the pattern gets set — and you've been avoiding the pen.
cells.ask: Release one thing you've been keeping that has already ended — honor the ending, and let the structure rebuild itself from what actually wants to continue. What comes back is direction that moves from genuine feeling, not from waiting for certainty.
cells.core: You've stopped building. Somewhere behind you is a room where the last structure didn't hold, or did and you didn't notice, and you've been taking instructions from that room ever since. The drive hasn't gone anywhere — the tending has. You're not in the present with the thing you're supposed to be keeping alive, and the fire is down to embers. Not because you lacked the capacity, but because you've been waiting to arrive.
cells.sheetLine: You're still waiting at a door that closed, and the fire has been waiting with you.

cells.tense: You're writing it now — setting the pattern, tending the fire — and you talk about it like it's happening on its own.
cells.verb: Keeping the structure standing — your structure, the one you built — while calling it just how things are.
cells.place: Where the pattern gets set — the room you fill, the shape you hold, without owning the pen.
cells.ask: Say "this is mine" about one structure you've been maintaining, and let the simpler truth of that stand. What comes back is breakthrough from genuine insight — the structures that needed to fall will fall, because you'll finally be the one deciding.
cells.core: You're already the one setting the pattern. The room holds together because you hold it, the fire burns because you tend it, and the structure works because you built it. But you tell the story as if it were the work doing that, or the circumstance, or the team. The writing is happening. You just haven't put your name on it. You've been keeping alive a thing you haven't admitted you made.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one holding it together. You haven't said so.
